EV-EVSE Assignment In the Platinum SCM, the EVSE assignment is made by forecasting the vehicle’s dwell time at arrival, or equivalently its departure time. If the dwell time is long enough to charge with a 25- kW charger, the EV is assigned to it; otherwise it gets assigned to a 350-kW charger to speed up the charge. In case there is a waiting queue for the 350-kW chargers (25-kW chargers do not have a queue), the SCM will sort the available EVSE by lowest queue and then highest vehicle SOC. 7 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. EVSE and BESS Dispatch The EVSE curtailment and BESS dispatch are achieved by a combination of predictive (feedforward) control and real-time implementation (feedback control). The predictive control uses accurate forecasts within a mixed-integer linear programming optimization problem to calculate the optimal EVSE power set points and target net grid demand required for all vehicles to reach their target SOC before their next rental and to minimize violations of the distribution grid capacity. The EVSE set points are referenced in real time, while the target net demand from the grid—also an output of the optimization—is used to update the baseline peak shaving threshold of the BESS, . Then, after measuring the current net load , the BESS will be dispatched to absorb any error from .
